[PATH:literature] Survey of recent literature on causal representation learning and self-supervised causal discovery (e.g., works by Bengio, Schölkopf, or Ke et al.) to identify whether any unsupervised or weakly-supervised methods have successfully scaled to high-dimensional inputs. — Provides a comprehensive view of the state-of-the-art, clarifying whether the hypothesized gap truly exists or has been addressed by recent advances.

C006.subject: Integration of causal reasoning modules into current AI architectures
C006.object: a decoupling of perception and reasoning pathways to achieve discontinuous improvement in out-of-distribution generalization
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Integration of causal reasoning modules into current AI architectures a decoupling of perception and reasoning pathways to achieve discontinuous improvement in out-of-distribution generalization]

[PATH:empirical] Ablation study comparing OOD generalization performance of a current SOTA architecture (e.g., a transformer-based vision model) with and without an integrated causal reasoning module (e.g., a structural causal model head), while keeping perception and reasoning pathways tightly coupled (i.e., shared representations). — If the integrated causal module yields a discontinuous improvement in OOD generalization without decoupling perception and reasoning, this would confirm the hypothesis. If no such improvement is observed, or if improvement only occurs after decoupling, the hypothesis is refuted.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the computational requirements for causal inference in neural architectures, focusing on whether shared representations between perception and reasoning necessarily limit out-of-distribution generalization due to confounding or shortcut learning. — If theory shows that decoupling is mathematically necessary to achieve invariant causal mechanisms (e.g., via independent causal mechanisms principle), the hypothesis is weakened. If theory shows that integrated modules can achieve the same invariance under certain conditions, the hypothesis is supported.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of existing empirical studies on causal representation learning for OOD generalization (e.g., works by Schölkopf, Bengio, or Peters) that explicitly test the effect of pathway separation on generalization discontinuities. — If the literature contains replicated evidence that discontinuous OOD gains only occur when perception and reasoning are decoupled (e.g., in object-centric or disentangled representation learning), the hypothesis is refuted. If studies show gains from causal modules without such decoupling, the hypothesis is confirmed.

qualifier.temporal: as of current state-of-the-art architectures in 2025
